combinations.name: White
combinations.goal: Peace — a world in which suffering has been designed out.
combinations.means: Order: rules, coordination, shared restraint, and the willingness to hold oneself to them.
combinations.guiding_question: What is the right thing to do here?

traits.name: Sense of Duty
traits.description: Treats an obligation as binding even when nobody is watching and nothing is gained by keeping it.

traits.name: Protectiveness
traits.description: Puts itself between the vulnerable and whatever threatens them, without being asked to.

traits.name: Fairness
traits.description: Applies to itself the same standard it asks of everyone else, and expects that to be reciprocated.

traits.name: Self-Righteousness
traits.description: Mistakes its own moral framework for the moral framework, and has trouble stepping outside it.

traits.name: Intolerance of Ambiguity
traits.description: Struggles wherever a situation refuses to sort itself into clear categories; under pressure it forces the pieces to fit.

traits.name: Formality
traits.description: Prefers explicit forms, stated expectations and named procedures to improvisation.

traits.name: Systematic Planning
traits.description: Wants the pieces mapped out and fitted together before anyone starts building.

traits.name: Proceduralism
traits.description: Keeps following the procedure past the point where it still serves the purpose it was written for.

traits.name: Devotion to Community
traits.description: Measures a choice by what it does for the group rather than by what it does for oneself.

traits.name: Deference to Tradition
traits.description: Trusts an inherited practice partly on the grounds that it has already lasted a long time.

combinations.name: Blue
combinations.goal: Perfection — the best version of a thing, reached once it is fully understood.
combinations.means: Knowledge: study, analysis, and the patient application of whatever has been learned.
combinations.guiding_question: What does careful thought say is the sensible move?

traits.name: Curiosity
traits.description: Wants to know how something works whether or not the answer will ever be useful.

traits.name: Rigour
traits.description: Checks its own reasoning before it trusts the conclusion.

traits.name: Foresight
traits.description: Plays out the consequences several steps past the move currently on the table.

traits.name: Analysis Paralysis
traits.description: Keeps collecting information long after enough of it was available to decide — often to avoid the decision.

traits.name: Dismissal of the Unmeasurable
traits.description: Treats whatever resists explanation or measurement as though it were not quite real.

traits.name: Detachment
traits.description: Steps back from a situation in order to see it clearly, at the price of no longer being inside it.

traits.name: Love of Elegant Systems
traits.description: Takes real pleasure in a structure where every part has exactly one clear job.

traits.name: Pedantry
traits.description: Insists on the exact formulation in situations where the rough one would have done fine.

traits.name: Subtlety
traits.description: Prefers the indirect move that leaves everyone else unsure what actually happened.

traits.name: Aloofness
traits.description: Holds a distance that reads as superiority, whether or not it was meant that way.

combinations.name: Black
combinations.goal: Satisfaction — actually getting what one wants, rather than what one is supposed to want.
combinations.means: Ruthlessness: accepting whatever a goal costs, and recognising no limit that does not come from one's own interests.

traits.name: Ambition
traits.description: Wants more, and says so, instead of pretending the wanting isn't there.

traits.name: Self-Reliance
traits.description: Assumes that whatever needs doing will end up having to be done by oneself, and plans on that basis.

traits.name: Decisiveness
traits.description: Commits to a course while everyone else is still weighing it.

traits.name: Ruthlessness
traits.description: Treats other people as terrain to be crossed rather than as ends in their own right.

traits.name: Short-Term Transactionalism
traits.description: Under pressure, refuses any investment that does not visibly pay back at once — often driving off exactly the help it needed.

traits.name: Amorality
traits.description: Does not experience morality as a real constraint; it neither obeys it nor rebels against it.

traits.name: Calculation
traits.description: Works out where an action leads before taking it, and picks the one that lands best.

traits.name: Manipulativeness
traits.description: Arranges what other people know so that they choose what it wanted them to choose.

traits.name: Insistence on Autonomy
traits.description: Will pay a real price rather than let anyone else hold the reins.

traits.name: Impatience with Obligation
traits.description: Feels being depended upon as a cage, and starts pulling away from it.

combinations.name: Red
combinations.goal: Freedom — room to follow whatever feels most alive.
combinations.means: Action: doing the thing now, in the moment, instead of deliberating about it first.
combinations.guiding_question: What do I actually want to do right now?

traits.name: Passion
traits.description: Throws its whole self at whatever it currently cares about.

traits.name: Spontaneity
traits.description: Acts on an impulse while it is still warm, rather than filing it away for later.

traits.name: Empathy
traits.description: Picks up what another person is feeling quickly, without needing it explained.

traits.name: Recklessness
traits.description: Commits before it has looked at what the commitment will cost.

traits.name: Volatility
traits.description: Under strain it amplifies its own feelings and then follows them, treating the intensity itself as justification.

traits.name: Restlessness
traits.description: Cannot sit for long in quiet, emptiness or boredom without needing to break it.

traits.name: Defiance
traits.description: Pushes back the moment something starts to feel like coercion.

traits.name: Fear of Commitment
traits.description: Avoids settling on anything, because settling closes off the futures it did not pick.

traits.name: Candour
traits.description: Says the true thing plainly, without arranging it first.

traits.name: Guilelessness
traits.description: Has no second layer — what it shows is what it is.

combinations.name: Green
combinations.goal: Harmony — being at peace with the world roughly as it already is.
combinations.means: Acceptance: taking up one's place in the existing order rather than trying to remake it.
combinations.guiding_question: How has this always been done, and what did that wisdom know?

traits.name: Serenity
traits.description: Stays steady when things go badly, because it never expected the world to be otherwise.

traits.name: Humility
traits.description: Assumes a long-standing arrangement probably knows something it does not yet know.

traits.name: Groundedness
traits.description: Stays attached to what is actually in front of it rather than to the version it planned for.

traits.name: Passivity
traits.description: Lets a situation run its course even where acting would clearly have helped.

traits.name: Fatalism
traits.description: Takes what happened as what had to happen, and stops looking for the alternative.

traits.name: Conservatism
traits.description: Wants a strong reason before anything established gets changed.

traits.name: Instinctiveness
traits.description: Trusts its gut reading of a situation over the argued one.

traits.name: Feralness
traits.description: Is comfortable outside the civilised frame and not embarrassed about it.

traits.name: Stewardship
traits.description: Looks after something it expects to hand on to whoever comes next.

traits.name: Insistence on Roles
traits.description: Has a place ready for everyone, and takes it badly when someone refuses to occupy theirs.

combinations.name: Azorius
combinations.guiding_question: How do we work out what is right — and show our working?

traits.name: Design Mindset
traits.description: Believes almost any problem gives way to a well-drawn structure, and reaches for one first.

traits.name: Procedural Fairness
traits.description: Trusts a rule that binds everyone equally more than a judgement made case by case.

traits.name: Bureaucratic Drift
traits.description: Ends up serving the process it built instead of the purpose it built the process for.

combinations.name: Dimir
combinations.guiding_question: What is the most effective route to what I want?

traits.name: Growth Mindset
traits.description: Refuses to treat its origins, or the role society has ready for it, as a ceiling.

traits.name: Enlightened Self-Interest
traits.description: Cooperates readily — because cooperating pays, not because it is owed.

traits.name: Arrogance
traits.description: Quietly assumes that whatever it has not yet grasped was probably not worth grasping.

combinations.name: Rakdos
combinations.guiding_question: What is standing between me and what I want?

traits.name: Fierce Autonomy
traits.description: Defends its own room to move, and grants everyone else the same by default.

traits.name: Unapologetic Appetite
traits.description: Wants what it wants openly, including the wants other people would rather not hear named.

traits.name: Disregard for Consequences
traits.description: Discounts the bill that arrives later against the thing that is available now.

combinations.name: Gruul
combinations.guiding_question: Where am I really, and where is this pulling me?

traits.name: Authenticity
traits.description: Would rather be disliked as itself than accepted as something it is not.

traits.name: Presence
traits.description: Is genuinely here — in this moment, with these people, without a frame in the way.

traits.name: Suspicion of Abstraction
traits.description: Distrusts an argument partly for being an argument, and misses the good ones along with the bad.

combinations.name: Selesnya
combinations.guiding_question: What is fair here, and what will still be standing in a generation?

traits.name: Sense of the Common Good
traits.description: Takes for granted that some things are worth more than one's own share of them.

traits.name: Sustaining Care
traits.description: Keeps the ordinary web of obligations and small kindnesses in working repair.

traits.name: Lost Purpose
traits.description: Carries on the good work long after it stopped checking whether the work still does good.

combinations.name: Orzhov
combinations.guiding_question: Who counts as one of us?

perspectives.text: Reads the disagreement as good against evil: whoever puts themselves above the group has simply defected on everyone else.
Reads it as sovereignty against dependency: a group has to earn allegiance, and one that demands it for free is coercing.
Whether the individual exists to serve the group or the group exists to serve the individual — which of the two is owed the sacrifice.

combinations.name: Boros
combinations.guiding_question: What needs doing here — and what would a decent person do about it?

perspectives.text: Reads the disagreement as order against chaos: without commitments that hold, nothing can be relied on and no trust can be built.
Reads it as freedom against constraint: every standing rule is one more thing nobody chose, narrowing who one is still allowed to become.
Structure against flexibility — the same arrangement looks like scaffolding from one side and like a cage from the other.

combinations.name: Izzet
combinations.guiding_question: What could exist that does not exist yet?

perspectives.text: Reads the disagreement as thinking clearly against reacting on the first impulse and calling it insight.
Reads it as being warmly alive against being so guarded that nothing gets felt and nothing gets done.
Reason and feeling, each claiming to be the more trustworthy guide to what one should actually do.

combinations.name: Simic
combinations.guiding_question: What am I still not seeing?

perspectives.text: Reads the disagreement as improvement against complacency: a system that has been understood is a system that can be made better.
Reads it as equilibrium against destabilisation: pulling on a thread nobody understands unravels more than it ever repairs.
How much of what a person becomes was settled by nature and circumstance, and how much of it is still genuinely open.

combinations.name: Golgari
combinations.guiding_question: What will this really cost, and who ends up paying it?

perspectives.text: Reads the disagreement as putting things to use against leaving them to rot untouched out of squeamishness.
Reads it as protecting a living balance against strip-mining it for a gain that will not last.
Take what the world offers, or leave it standing — the argument over what the individual owes the environment it grew out of.
